lawyer:
SM Zahidur Rahman, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 
Shamim Ara Dora, Assistant Attorney-General—For the Opposite Party.
parties:
SM Zahidur Rahman ------ Petitioner  
vs
State ------ Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
AFM Abdur Rahman J: The learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman obtained this Rule on 16-2-1988 under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, challenging the legality and propriety of the Order No. 14 dated 24-12-1987, passed by Mr Md Azizul Haque, Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, in Criminal Miscellaneous (Bail) Case No. 287 of 1987 forfeiting the bail bond furnished by the petitioner Mk SM Zahidur Rahman as Advocate surety. At the time of issuance of the Rule all further proceeding in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 287 of 1987 (Bail) pending as aforesaid, has been stayed by this Division. 

 2. One Kumar Biswas was implicated in Bagerhat Police Station Case No. 14 dated 21-4-1987 under section 120 (Kha)/302/34 of the Penal Code and upon his failure to obtain enlargement on bail from the Court of Magistrate, First Class, Bagerhat, accused Shib Kumar Biswas preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 287 of 1987 (Bail) before the Court of Sessions Judge, Bagerhat on 26-7-1987 praying for enlargement on bail. The learned Additional Sessions Judge Mr MA Matin upon registering the said miscellaneous case called for the records from the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Bagerhat and rejected the prayer for enlargement on ad-interim bail for the time being. Thereafter, on 13-8-1987, when the LCR reached the said Court on 18-8-1987, the learned Additional Sessions Judge Mr MA Matin, being satisfied as to the requirement of the accused to be enlarged on bail, passed his order enlarging the said accused on ad-interim bail of Taka 50,000 with two sureties of like amount, one of whom shall be a practicing Advocate of the local Bar and the other local surety should be the Upazila Chairman or Chairman of the Union Parishad. 

 4. As the bail was taken for the said accused in ad-interim form, the same was awaiting confirmation but the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, could not hear the confirmation of bail matter till 13-11-1987 due to his engagement in conducting the hearing of the other matter before him. The aforesaid bail matter thereafter came before the learned Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, presided over by Mr Azizul Haque, who finding the accused Shib Kumar Biswas absent in the case on the said date passed order No. 12 dated 30-11-1987 with the following direction; 

 6. Thereafter, the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 441 of 1987 under the provision of section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure has been initiated by the learned Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, against the local surety Mr MA Awal and the Advocate surety Mr SM Zahidur Rahman, Advocate and the learned Court passed order No. 15 dated 26-12-1987 directing the sureties to deposit the forfeited amount in the Court. Thereafter, on subsequent two occasions on 7-1-1988 and 24-1-1988 the learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman filed petitions praying for time to produce the absconding accused person before the Court, but the learned Sessions Judge on 24-1-1988 issued distress warrant under the provision of section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure against the sureties of the bail bond including the Advocate surety. 

 10. The learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman submits that the learned practicing Advocates of the local Bar having been duty bound, by the nature of the profession, to stand surety in favour of the accused persons, when bail has been granted in favour of the accused, for the learned Advocate is engaged in their cases, and, as such, a long standing practice has cropped up in the Sub-continent to take lenient view about the Advocate surety of the accused who absconds after the enlargement on bail and practically, the local sureties are made primarily liable to produce the absconding accused person before the Court. The learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman, in support of the Rule, strenuously argued that a series of decisions of this Division have established the principle that neither too rigid nor too lenient a view should be taken against the Advocate surety who executed bond in favour of an absconded accused in order to keep up the practice of the learned Advocate in the Mofussil Bar. In this context the learned Advocate referred the case of Al-Zahirul Haque vs State reported in 1949 PLD Dhaka 31. The learned Advocate prays for making the Rule absolute. 

 12. We have heard the learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman, in person, and the learned Assistant Attorney-General. We have perused the order sheet of Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 287 of 1987 (Bail) and 441 of 1987, appended as Annexure to the application and other materials on record. 

 13. It appears that the accused Shib Kumar Biswas, having failed to obtain enlargement on bail from the Magistrate, First Class, Bagerhat, preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 287 of 1987 (Bail) before the Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, on 26-7-1987 which was heard by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-in-charge of the Session Court, Mr Md A Matin, who rejected the prayer for enlargement of the accused-person on ad-interim bail and called for the LCR from the Magistrate, First Class, Bagerhat. Thereafter, upon receiving the lower Courts record, on 13-8-1987 the Additional Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, Mr Md A Matin, enlarged the accused person Shib Kumar Biswas on ad-interim bail by his order No. 2 dated 13-8-1987, pursuant to which the learned Advocate Mr SM Zahidur Rahman stood Advocate surety on behalf of the accused person executing the same and making him liable to pay an amount of Taka 50,000 to the Court in default of the accused person to turn up before the Court. 

 14. As the bail has been taken in ad-interim form from the accused person, the Additional Sessions Judge, Bagerhat accepted the bail bond by itself which impliedly meant that the accused person shall appear before the Court of Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, till the bail is confirmed and the accused person executes a bail bond in favour of the trial Court. It appears that the accused person Shib Kumar Biswas filed hajira on 18-8-1987 before the Sessions Judge, Bagerhat in Miscellaneous Case No. 247 of 1987 (Bail) which was at that time presided over by Mr Azizul Haque, Sessions Judge, Bagerhat. Thereafter, also on the next two dates, fixed on 9-9-1987 and 26-9-1987, the accused person filed hajira before the said Court. But later the accused person did not file any hajira before that Court on 14-11-1987 and it further appears from the order sheet dated 14-11-1987 that on that date there was hartal observed all over Bangladesh. Thereafter, on the next date, fixed on 15-12-1987, the learned Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, Mr Md Azizul Haque, passed the order issuing warrant of arrest against the accused person and also directed the sureties of the bail bond to show cause as to why the bond money shall not be forfeited. It appears to us that the learned Sessions Judge Mr Azizul Haque has been harsh in passing such an order directing the surety of the bail bond to show cause as to why the bond amount shall not be forfeited, since the legal practice required an Advocate to stand surety in favour of an accused person whose case he was dealing before the particular Court and if a rigid view is taken in respect of the failure of the Advocate surety to produce the absconding accused instead of penalising the local surety, the long standing practice of standing Advocate surety in favour of the accused person will be jeopardized for which their Lordships in the Apex Court have already decided to take a lenient view in a case against the Advocate surety where the accused has absconded. 

 15. We have considered the contention of Mr SM Zahidur Rahman and the referred case of Al-Zahid vs State reported in 1993 BLD 275 wherein his Lordship Baker J, as his Lordship was then, in an identical question raised before him has taken the view that in order to uphold the legal profession and the norm, which has been established through long transaction, a lenient view should be taken in such case. It was thereafter held in that case; 

 "Further, it will not do to forget that these lawyer sureties also fulfill certain genuine requirements of our social system. To be too harsh to them would mean that an accused may be reduced to the position of not getting a surety in very hard and genuine cases. We cannot afford to be too harsh or to liberal to them and we should take a middle course". 

 16. In the case of Syed Moazzem Hossain and others vs State reported in 13 DLR 726 his Lordship Mr Baker J, as his Lordship was then, again on the point that which Court can forfeit the bail bonds as executed by sureties, examined the nature of bail bond and held as under; 

 It was contended on behalf of the surety that the bond to produce the accused having been executed before the Senior Special Judge it could not be forfeited for failure to produce the accused before another judge, namely, the Special Judge to whom the case was transferred for trial. The bond was headed as "in the Court of Special Judge, Dinajpur". 

 18. The aforesaid bail bond has clearly manifest that the same has been executed in favour of the Magistrate, First Class, Bagerhat although the same has been accepted by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, Md A Matin on 16-8-1987. The legal implication of bail bond is nothing but contractual agreement between the Court and the accused person wherein the sureties of the bond would take the liability of producing the accused person of the case in the Court at the time of hearing or to the transferee Court where the case may be transferred for trial. Therefore, the forfeiture of the bond on the ground that the accused person failed to turn up before the Court may be made by the Court in whose favour the bond has been executed. In the case before us although the statement made in the body of the bail bond manifests that the same has been executed in favour of the Magistrate 1st Class, Bagerhat, which appears to be an erroneous statement as the bond was actually executed against taking of ad-interim bail by the Sessions Judge, Bagerhat and, as such, the learned Session Judge was required to examine the bond before forfeiting the same to satisfy itself whether the contractual agreement by way of bail bond was unambiguous and clear as to its manifestation of its liability. Such a failure of the learned Session Judge, Bagerhat, compelled us to hold that the forfeiture of the bond amount of the learned Advocate surety was not lawful which is liable to be interfered with by this Court. 

 21. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The very direction passed by the learned Sessions Judge Mr Md Azizul Haque in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No 441 of 1987, under section 514 of the Code of Criminal Procedure being not sustainable in law, is hereby set aside. The learned Advocate surety Mr SM Zahidur Rahman is hereby exonerated from the liability of the bail bond as executed by him in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No 287 of 1987 (Bail) before the Sessions Judge, Bagerhat. The distress warrant, as issued by the learned Sessions Judge, Bagerhat, for realisation of the forfeited amount of Taka 50,000 from the learned Advocate surety of SM Zahidur Rahman is hereby recalled.
